original_question: Problem 7.9 (Á. Pelayo). Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system T1,~ , . . . , Tn,~ that a singularity is degenerate?
target_in_paper: §7.2, Problem 7.9 (Á. Pelayo): "Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} that a singularity is degenerate?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact official open problem essentially verbatim: it identifies the correct section-level topic (inverse spectral questions for quantum integrable systems), the correct attribution (Á. Pelayo), the correct object of study (the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system), and the exact issue asked in the paper (whether degeneracy of a singularity can be detected spectrally).
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should specify that T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} are semiclassical self-adjoint commuting operators, i.e. a quantum integrable system in the sense defined in §7.1.
It should identify the associated classical integrable system: the principal symbols f_1,\ldots,f_n of T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} define F=(f_1,\ldots,f_n) on a symplectic manifold (M,\omega).

It should clarify that the singularity whose degeneracy is to be detected is a singularity of the classical integrable system / singular Lagrangian fibration associated with F, not of the quantum operators themselves.
The surrounding context makes clear that the relevant spectral data are considered in the semiclassical regime \hbar \to 0; the draft does not state that explicitly.
For complete self-containment, 'joint spectrum' should be understood as the set of simultaneous eigenvalue n-tuples of the commuting operators T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar}.
For complete self-containment, 'degenerate' should be read in the integrable-systems sense: not nondegenerate as a singularity of the classical moment map F.

The paper does not impose extra restrictions here such as toric or semitoric, fixed dimension, fixed rank, or a specific quantization model beyond the general semiclassical framework of §7.1; adding such restrictions would move away from the paper's actual scope.
refined_question: Let T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} be a quantum integrable system in the sense of §7.1, i.e. commuting self-adjoint semiclassical operators on a quantum Hilbert space whose principal symbols f_1,\ldots,f_n are almost everywhere independent on a symplectic manifold (M,\omega). From the joint spectrum of T_{1,\hbar},\ldots,T_{n,\hbar} in the semiclassical limit \hbar\to 0, can one determine whether a singularity of the associated classical integrable system F=(f_1,\ldots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n is degenerate rather than nondegenerate?
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact official target: Problem 7.9 in §7.2. The only sharpening needed is to make explicit the classical object to which 'degenerate singularity' refers and the semiclassical meaning of the spectral data. Those clarifications come from the §7.1 definition of quantum integrable systems and from the surrounding inverse-spectral discussion in §7.2: Conjecture 7.5 and Problem 7.8 frame the broader program of recovering classical data from semiclassical joint spectra, and the paper explicitly says that Problem 7.9 is closely related to Question 2.5 on recovering singularity type from asymptotic behavior near singular fibres.
